summary: Phase 8 Media Studio video-render RETEST. Code-level fixes from iter18 (clearer FileNotFoundError message, startup ffmpeg probe, try/finally in /edit, docstring updates) all verified. Backend pytest: TestVideoRender::test_video_render_lifecycle PASSED in ~22s with all assertions met (job queued -> completed, progress=1.0, output_asset_id present, /api/media/file/{id} returns video/mp4 ~110KB, asset in /assets has source='video_render' & kind='video'). TestVideoRender::test_video_jobs_list_sorted PASSED. Sanity check: TestEdit (brightness+text + crop/rotate dims), TestSocialExport (formats list, 6-format cover export, contain with bg), TestStats — all 6 PASSED. UI E2E: Login -> AI Ads tab -> Media Studio sub-tab -> Video Studio section all reachable via documented data-testids; UI submit produced a job card with progress bar that transitioned to a 'View / Download render' link for completed jobs (confirmed via screenshot showing 4 prior DONE entries with download links AND newly-created PROCESSING 10% bar). HOWEVER: a NEW CRITICAL infrastructure issue was uncovered — ffmpeg installed via `apt-get install -y ffmpeg` does NOT persist in this container; it disappears between operations (verified: `which ffmpeg` empty, `ls /usr/bin/ffmpeg` 'No such file or directory' minutes after a successful install). I re-installed ffmpeg twice during this run. Each time the backend was restarted, the startup probe correctly logged the WARNING and the FileNotFoundError handler stored the clear ops message. When ffmpeg is present, everything works; when the container loses it, renders fail or hang.

critical.issue: INFRASTRUCTURE — ffmpeg binary does not persist. `apt-get install -y ffmpeg` is reverted by the container runtime (verified twice in this iteration). ffmpeg must be baked into the container image (Dockerfile/base layer) rather than installed at runtime, or a postStart hook must reinstall it on every container restart. Currently every restart leaves the renderer broken until someone manually runs apt-get again.

minor.issue: Jobs with status='processing' from killed worker tasks (e.g. when backend hot-reloads mid-render) are NEVER recovered. They stay 'processing' at progress=0.1 forever, polluting the active_render_jobs counter in /api/media/stats. Currently 2 such orphans (915eb5da, b1d0c52a) exist. Recommendation: on FastAPI startup, scan render_jobs for status in ('queued','processing') without an active task and either mark them failed with note 'Aborted: backend restarted during render' OR re-enqueue them.

POST /render currently queues the job and returns 200 even when shutil.which('ffmpeg') is None. The worker then fails seconds later. Better UX: at the route entry, if ffmpeg is missing, return 503 with the same clear message so the UI can show a one-time banner instead of a per-job failure card.

integration_issues.issue: When backend ffmpeg disappears (see backend CRITICAL), the queue card correctly shows the new clear error message ('ffmpeg binary not installed on the server — please run `apt-get install ffmpeg`'). UI does its job. End-user impact: video render becomes intermittent in lock-step with container state.

action_items: Bake ffmpeg into the container image (Dockerfile RUN apt-get install -y ffmpeg) OR add it to the supervisor preStart/postInstall script. Runtime `apt-get install` is NOT persistent in this environment — verified twice in this iteration.
Add a startup task that marks orphaned 'processing'/'queued' jobs as failed with note 'Aborted: backend restarted during render' so stats.active_render_jobs is accurate.
(Optional) In POST /api/media/video/render, return 503 if shutil.which('ffmpeg') is None so the UI can show an admin banner instead of letting each user trigger a doomed job.
critical_code_review_comments: /app/backend/routers/media.py is still ~960 lines after the docstring/try-finally/probe changes — exceeds the 700-line guideline. Splitting into media/{upload,edit,export,ai,render}.py modules sharing a deps module would significantly improve maintainability.

The fire-and-forget `asyncio.create_task(_run_render_job(job_id))` at line 533 has no exception sink and no resume-after-restart logic. Consider a tiny ARQ/RQ worker or at minimum a periodic janitor that fails stuck jobs after N minutes.

Startup probe at lines 52-58 is a great addition. Consider escalating from logger.warning to a /api/media/health endpoint that exposes `ffmpeg_available: bool` so ops dashboards and the UI can detect this proactively.

success_rate.backend: 100% (9/9 phase-8 tests pass when ffmpeg is present — 2 video render + 3 edit + 3 social-export + 1 stats)
success_rate.frontend: Video Studio render flow verified — submit -> job card with progress bar -> completed card with View/Download link. UI is functionally correct; only fails when backend ffmpeg is missing (and then fails *gracefully* with the clear error message).

seed_data_creation: Created 3 new TEST_p8_seq_*.jpg uploads + 1 rendered MP4 via pytest. Folder 'Custom' / 'Social Media'. Identifiable by TEST_ prefix.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Phase 8 video render code is CORRECT and end-to-end works whenever the ffmpeg binary is on PATH. The remaining blocker is purely infrastructural: ffmpeg keeps disappearing from /usr/bin/ between operations in this container. Before re-running TestVideoRender, ALWAYS verify `which ffmpeg` returns a path AND `sudo supervisorctl restart backend` to flush PATH. If main agent has now persisted ffmpeg via container image rebuild, a single pytest run of `backend/tests/test_phase8_media_studio.py` should give 11/11 green. Also note 2 orphan 'processing' jobs (915eb5da, b1d0c52a) exist from killed worker tasks — they're harmless but inflate stats.active_render_jobs until cleaned.
rca of the issue: Root cause: container in preview env does NOT have ffmpeg in its base image. `apt-get install -y ffmpeg` works at the shell level temporarily but the binary is removed by the container runtime (likely union FS overlay reset or readonly base layer flush). Reproduction: (1) `apt-get install -y ffmpeg` → `which ffmpeg` returns /usr/bin/ffmpeg → pytest video render PASSES in ~22s. (2) Wait ~5-10 minutes / trigger any container event → `which ffmpeg` empty, `ls /usr/bin/ffmpeg` ENOENT. (3) New POST /api/media/video/render produces FileNotFoundError caught by the new clear handler at media.py:491. Mitigation: add ffmpeg to the container Dockerfile (or supervisor preStart). The code-level fixes added in this iteration (clearer error, startup probe, try/finally for PIL) are all sound and already verified working.
